title: Fourier coefficient and polynomial root probability
statement: Let $\ell\ne0$, let $\gamma$ be a $d$-coordinate binary vector, and let $a$ assign to each element $r$ of the degree-$\ell$ extension field of $\mathbb{F}_2$ a $d$-tuple of field elements. Let $p$ be a nonzero polynomial over that field whose value at every $r$ equals the field sum of the coordinates of $\gamma$ multiplied by the corresponding entries of $a(r)$. Then the vector Fourier coefficient of the density generated by the field pairing is the number of roots of $p$ in the extension field divided by $2^\ell$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ maps each field element to a $d$-tuple of field elements
$p$ is a nonzero polynomial over the extension field
For every field element $r$, $p(r)$ equals the stated field pairing
